Introduction sec:intro The rapid evolution of digital human technologies is transforming immersive interaction across augmented and virtual reality, telepresence, gaming, and social communication. This progress has been driven by the combination of parametric human models, such as FLAME~ FLAME:SiggraphAsia2017 for faces, SMPL~ SMPL:2015 and SMPL-X~ SMPL-X:2019 for bodies, and MANO~ MANO:SIGGRAPHASIA:2017 for hands, with high-fidelity neural rendering techniques including NeRF~ mildenhall2020nerf and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)~ kerbl2023gaussiansplatting . Among these components, hands play a central role as the primary interface for fine-grained interaction and dexterous manipulation~ tzionas2016capturing, hasson19_obman, GRAB:2020, chao:cvpr2021, sayem2026handvqa . However, despite their importance, creating personalized, animatable, and photorealistic hand avatars from minimal input remains a key challenge for scalable digital human systems. While substantial progress has been made in single-image 3D avatar reconstruction for head avatars~ chu2024gpavatar, chu2024gagavatar, he2025lam and full-body avatars~ zhuang2024idolinstant, qiu2025anigs, qiu2025LHM, sim2025persona , high-fidelity hand avatar modeling from a single image remains comparatively underexplored and particularly challenging. Hands are highly articulated, thin, and frequently self-occluded~ tzionas2016capturing, zb2017hand, hasson19_obman , which makes reconstruction from sparse observations inherently ill-posed. Existing hand avatar pipelines address this ill-posedness through additional observations or per-subject optimization. Most methods rely on multi-view capture or monocular video with subject-specific fitting~ handavatar, mundra2023livehand, karunratanakul2023harp ; single-image approaches still require optimization-based inversion at inference~ zheng2024ohta ; and Gaussian-based methods remain dependent on multi-view or video-based reconstruction~ Zhao2025GaussianHand . Consequently, scalable single-image hand avatar reconstruction without test-time optimization remains largely unresolved. To eliminate the dependence on dense observations and costly test-time optimization, we aim to directly predict an animatable hand avatar from a single image, given off-the-shelf MANO, camera, and mask estimates, in a feed-forward manner. We adopt 3DGS~ kerbl2023gaussiansplatting, ali2026compression as the output representation for its efficient rendering and controllable geometry and appearance. However, feed-forward Gaussian avatar methods developed for heads~ he2025lam and bodies~ qiu2025LHM do not transfer directly to hands. First, hands are thin, low-volume, and highly articulated, so even minor errors in Gaussian position, scale, or orientation produce over-expanded or overlapping primitives, thickness artifacts, and degraded fidelity under novel poses. Second, appearance from a single image is ambiguous: existing feed-forward pipelines~ he2025lam, qiu2025LHM regress appearance directly from image features and tend to fall back on learned priors even in observed regions, weakening input-specific cues such as skin tone and fine texture, while unobserved regions must still be completed plausibly. Feed-forward hand avatar reconstruction therefore requires (i) geometry stabilization for thin, articulated structures and (ii) source-conditioned appearance modeling that preserves reliable input evidence while completing missing regions from priors. To address these challenges, we propose InstantHand (Fig.~ fig:hook ), a feed-forward 3DGS framework for single-image animatable hand avatar reconstruction. For geometry, we constrain Gaussian placement, scale, and orientation around MANO anchors and supervise rendered alpha on the silhouette band to keep thin fingers compact. For appearance, we introduce Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer, where Gaussians supported by input observations are selectively enhanced with reliable local appearance cues to preserve input-specific details such as skin tone and fine textures. For unobserved regions, appearance is inferred using the learned prior together with a global identity representation, enabling consistent completion under occlusion. Our contributions can be summarized as follows: 1pt 0pt We present InstantHand, a feed-forward framework that reconstructs an animatable canonical 3D Gaussian hand avatar from a single image without per-subject optimization. We propose a Soft Alpha Band (SAB) regularizer that concentrates alpha supervision on silhouette boundaries, reducing alpha leakage and preserving thin finger structures. We introduce Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer, which preserves observed appearance based on each Gaussian's rendering contribution while completing unobserved regions using the learned prior and a global source identity. InstantHand achieves reconstruction quality comparable to per-subject-optimized baselines and competitive zero-shot performance, with avatar construction in 2.84\,s and rendering at 161\,FPS. Related Work Hand Pose and Shape Estimation. Monocular 3D hand pose and mesh estimation provides the geometric foundation for many hand-centric vision systems~ baek2019pushing, baek2020weakly, Moon_2020_ECCV_I2L-MeshNet, lin2021metro, lin2021mesh_graphormer, 2022MobRecon, cho2023transformer, zhou2024simple, pavlakos2024hamer, dong2024hamba, ismayilzada2025qort, potamias2025wilor . These methods either predict mesh vertices directly or regress the parameters of the MANO model~ MANO:SIGGRAPHASIA:2017 from RGB images~ baek2019pushing, baek2020weakly . For example, METRO~ lin2021metro and Mesh Graphormer~ lin2021mesh_graphormer use transformers to regress the vertices of a MANO-topology hand mesh from a single image. More recent methods, including HaMeR~ pavlakos2024hamer and WiLoR~ potamias2025wilor , regress MANO parameters together with camera parameters from unconstrained images. Our work takes off-the-shelf pose, camera, and mask estimates as input and focuses on reconstructing and rendering an animatable hand avatar. Hand Avatar Reconstruction. Hand avatar reconstruction aims to recover subject-specific geometry and appearance for rendering under novel viewpoints and poses. Most existing approaches rely on multi-view images or monocular video sequences and employ neural implicit representations~ mildenhall2020nerf, haider2026inr or explicit mesh-based pipelines~ corona2022lisa,handavatar,mundra2023livehand,karunratanakul2023harp,guo2023handnerf,kalshetti2024intrinsichand . Representative methods include HandAvatar~ handavatar , HARP~ karunratanakul2023harp , and LiveHand~ mundra2023livehand , which adopt implicit, mesh-based, and multi-view neural rendering formulations, respectively. To reduce dependence on dense observations, single-image approaches such as OHTA~ zheng2024ohta incorporate learned priors for one-shot reconstruction, but still require test-time fitting or inversion. Gaussian-based methods, including GaussianHand~ Zhao2025GaussianHand , use explicit 3D Gaussian primitives for efficient rendering. As summarized in Table~ tab:method_comparison of the appendix, existing methods require either dense observations or per-subject optimization, regardless of representation. In contrast, our method constructs an animatable Gaussian hand avatar from a single image without test-time optimization. Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction. Feed-forward avatar methods predict the parameters of animatable 3D Gaussians from one or a few images, avoiding per-subject optimization. This approach has been applied to full- and upper-body avatars by LHM~ qiu2025LHM and GUAVA~ GUAVA , and to head avatars by GAGAvatar~ chu2024gagavatar and LAM~ he2025lam . However, reconstructing an animatable hand avatar from a single image remains challenging, as thin finger boundaries are sensitive to alpha leakage and the source view provides incomplete appearance information (Sec.~ sec:intro ; Appendix~ sec:supp_related ). We address these challenges with a Soft Alpha Band regularizer that targets boundary leakage and Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer that combines observed appearance with a learned prior and a global source identity. Method sec:method Given a single source image , InstantHand reconstructs an animatable 3D hand in a single forward pass (Fig.~ fig:pipeline ). Source-image features are fused with MANO-surface query anchors to form per-Gaussian tokens (Sec.~ sec:image_mano_fusion ), which parameterize a canonical Gaussian representation with surface-anchored centers, learned scales, and base colors, while opacity and canonical rotation remain fixed (Sec.~ sec:canonical_gs ). Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer then refines only the Gaussian colors using contribution-aware local evidence and a global source appearance identity (Sec.~ sec:source_conditioned_gaussian_appearance ). The resulting Gaussians are animated via MANO-driven deformation and rendered from arbitrary viewpoints. The two-stage training objective is described in Sec.~ sec:training_objective .
